headline: Your WindoVision waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing US and Canadian real estate offices into the right WindoVision storefront pitch. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for John Collman, President and CEO.
productSummary: WindoVision (TouchPoint Systems) turns a brokerage storefront into a 24/7 interactive listing and lead channel. Dual thru-glass touch, MLS/IDX sync, QR codes, exterior audio, and preferred-partner slots so walk-by traffic becomes email and text leads after hours. Installed across the US and Canada since 2002. Homepage and About: 900+ offices transformed, 30 million+ users reached, paper window listings replaced with live stock.
coreInsight: John already sells the always-on storefront. The one TAM is brick-and-mortar real estate offices Google Maps already lists. The one routing signal is what that same storefront shows today: paper flyers still taped in the window, a brand-new or renovating office, multi-office groups with uneven digital coverage, or every remaining in-TAM storefront. One Maps-plus-photo pass returns both the TAM and the route. Apollo is email last, never the spine.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is what the storefront window already shows
sections.takeaway: Google Maps Places plus Street View and listing photos already name the brick-and-mortar office and already show paper flyers, a renovation or opening, multi-office digital gaps, or none of those. That storefront_window_state is stronger than a title guess, and it is cheap to collect.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes every US and Canadian brokerage office
sections.takeaway: First match wins. Paper flyers still taped in the window go first, then brand-new or renovating offices, then multi-office groups with uneven digital coverage, then every remaining in-TAM storefront Maps still lists.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Each storefront state gets a different first offer
sections.takeaway: Paper-flyer offices get a Paper-to-Pixel Window Brief. New or renovating offices get a Fit-Out Storefront Kit. Multi-office groups get a Portfolio Coverage Map. The rest get the 24/7 Lead Window Playbook.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: Replace the paper, kit the fit-out, even the portfolio, then cover the rest
sections.takeaway: The list is always US and Canadian brick-and-mortar real estate offices, aimed at broker-owners, principals, and office managers. Franchise brand and city are merge tags, not a second TAM. A/Bs sit on the exclusive routes.

sections.label: Email Copy
sections.title: Copy that names the window Maps already shows
sections.takeaway: Notice the paper flyers, the opening, or the uneven digital coverage, poke the after-hours lead or stale-listing gap that state implies, then ask for a one-letter yes.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the paper-flyer offices first
sections.takeaway: Start where Street View still shows taped listings. Prove reply density, then roll renovation and opening offices, multi-office gaps, and the 24/7 Lead Window Playbook catch-all. Apollo is never the list spine.

signalReasons: Google Maps Places in the Real estate agency / Real estate office category is the TAM John already sells into: brick-and-mortar US and Canadian offices with a visible storefront. Public TAM account count is not published on windovision.com; do not invent a headcount. Keep each launch tier at the waterfall SOP contact floor where the TAM allows.

The same Maps pull plus Street View and listing photos returns storefront_window_state: paper flyers still taped in the window, a brand-new or renovating office, multi-office groups with uneven digital coverage, or none of those — enough to route without a second expensive enrichment product.

The ladder maps to live WindoVision copy on windovision.com: replace paper window listings with live MLS/IDX stock, kit a new or renovating storefront as a 24/7 listing and lead channel, even digital coverage across a group, then a soft 24/7 Lead Window Playbook for every remaining in-TAM office. Proof stays at published site numbers only: 900+ offices transformed, 30 million+ users reached, in market since 2002.
Franchise brand, city, and buyer title are scrape filters and merge tags. They are not a second waterfall. Apollo is email last after the office is routed, never the TAM spine.

sources.name: Google Maps Places + photos / Street View (Real estate agency, US and Canada)
sources.delivers: In-TAM brick-and-mortar offices plus the storefront_window_state used to assign Tier 1 / 2 / 3 / catch-all. The TAM gate and the spine of every route. One pull. Not Apollo.

sources.delivers: renovation_or_opening used for Tier 2: new office, remodel, relocation, or grand-opening language with no Tier-1 paper-flyer match.

sources.name: Agency website team / leadership page

routingRules.why: Already a WindoVision / TouchPoint customer office. A franchise brand in the gallery is not enough to exclude.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND paper_flyers = true (Street View or listing photos still show paper listing flyers taped in the window) AND not already_customer
routingRules.why: They are still running the paper window WindoVision was built to replace. Strongest intent. Homepage and About already contrast taped listings with live stock; Brad Whittaker's published quote names walk-ins frustrated that paper flyers were already pending or sold.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND renovation_or_opening = true (new office, remodel, relocation, or grand opening on Maps, site, or local news) AND no Tier-1 paper-flyer match AND not already_customer
routingRules.why: They are already spending on the physical office. Maps to WindoVision as the 24/7 listing and lead layer in the fit-out — dual thru-glass, MLS/IDX, QR, exterior audio — before the window defaults back to paper.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND multi_office_gap = true (same brand / group shows 2+ Maps listings and digital storefront coverage is uneven) AND no Tier 1-2 match AND not already_customer
routingRules.why: The group already bought a premium location somewhere and left other windows analog. A coverage map is the first offer: which offices still leak after-hours traffic, and where preferred-partner slots can offset cost.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND none of the above
routingRules.why: Still in TAM (US/Canada brick-and-mortar real estate offices Maps already lists). Soft CTA around after-hours email and text leads, live MLS/IDX stock, and a first conversation. Mandatory 100% coverage.

tiers.name: Tier 1
tiers.label: Paper flyers still in the window
tiers.trigger: Google Street View or Maps listing photos still show paper listing flyers taped in the storefront; not already a WindoVision customer
tiers.pain: Walk-by traffic still reads stale paper. Published client quote from Brad Whittaker (Realty ONE Group Pacifica): buyers were frustrated that other offices had listings taped up that were already pending or sold. After hours, the window generates zero email or text leads.
tiers.valueProp: Paper-to-Pixel Window Brief: replace taped flyers with a dual thru-glass display that syncs live MLS/IDX stock, QR codes, and after-hours email/text capture. Anchored to published site proof only: 900+ offices transformed, 30 million+ users reached.
tiers.dataSource: Google Maps Places + Street View / listing photos for paper flyers in the window
tiers.replyDensity: Highest - they already use the window as a listing channel

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: New, relocating, or renovating office
tiers.trigger: In-TAM office shows a new location, remodel, relocation, or grand opening on Maps, the site, or local news, with no Tier-1 paper-flyer match
tiers.pain: They are already writing a check for paint, glass, and furniture. If the window is not specified as a 24/7 listing and lead channel, it defaults back to paper the week they open.
tiers.valueProp: Fit-Out Storefront Kit: WindoVision as the specified storefront layer in the renovation — dual thru-glass, High Bright monitors, exterior audio, MLS/IDX, QR — so the new office opens as an always-on information center, not a taped-flyer window.
tiers.dataSource: Local news, permitting/opening coverage, Maps recency, and site language after the paper-flyer filter fails
tiers.replyDensity: High - visible spend window, clear install moment

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: Multi-office group with uneven digital coverage
tiers.trigger: Same brand or group shows 2+ Google listings and digital storefront coverage is uneven, with no Tier 1-2 match
tiers.pain: One office looks modern; the next still leaks nights and weekends. Preferred-partner inventory and after-hours capture do not roll across the group.
tiers.valueProp: Portfolio Coverage Map: which offices still run analog windows, where walk-by traffic is wasted after hours, and how preferred-partner slots on windovision.com can offset system cost across the group.
tiers.dataSource: Same-brand Places clustering (name + website + phone) plus photo pass for digital vs analog windows
tiers.replyDensity: Medium - clear group gap, longer multi-site cycle

tiers.name: Catch-all
tiers.label: Remaining in-TAM storefronts
tiers.trigger: Every remaining in-TAM US/Canada brick-and-mortar real estate office Maps already lists, with no Tier 1-3 storefront_window_state
tiers.pain: They still have glass on the street and still go dark after hours. Generic window vinyl or a dark office does not turn walk-bys into email and text leads.
tiers.valueProp: Soft 24/7 Lead Window Playbook: how peers turn unused window space into an always-on listing and lead channel — MLS/IDX sync, QR, exterior audio, preferred partners — using only published proof (900+ offices, 30 million+ users, since 2002). Soft CTA.
tiers.dataSource: Google Maps Places TAM after higher tiers route out

campaigns.name: Paper-to-Pixel Window Brief
campaigns.strategy: Name {{window_signal}} and contrast stale taped listings with live MLS/IDX stock plus after-hours email and text capture. Offer the Paper-to-Pixel Window Brief. Proof stays at 900+ offices and 30 million+ users. Use {{case_quote}} as an illustrative merge from published client language, not a new metric.

campaigns.name: After-hours lead variant
campaigns.filter: Same Tier 1 list, nights-and-weekends copy instead of stale-paper copy
campaigns.strategy: Keep {{window_signal}} in the notice line. Swap the poke to 24/7 email and text lead generation on the homepage — the window still works when the office is closed.
campaigns.overview: A/B against the paper-to-pixel brief. Same exclusive route, after-hours capture language instead of stale-flyer language.

campaigns.name: Fit-Out Storefront Kit
campaigns.strategy: Lead with {{opening_signal}}. Offer the Fit-Out Storefront Kit so the new or renovating office specifies dual thru-glass, MLS/IDX, QR, and exterior audio before the window defaults to paper.
campaigns.value: Specify the window in the fit-out
campaigns.overview: Second exclusive route. Opening and remodel angle.

campaigns.name: Set-the-storefront-apart variant
campaigns.strategy: Keep {{opening_signal}} in the first line. Lead with published client language that the display sets the storefront apart and engages the immediate community — not a new number.
campaigns.overview: A/B against the fit-out kit. Same waterfall tier, community and presence hook.

campaigns.name: Portfolio Coverage Map
campaigns.strategy: Lead with {{location_count}} and uneven digital windows across the group. Offer a Portfolio Coverage Map of which offices still leak after-hours traffic.
campaigns.value: Even digital coverage across the group
campaigns.overview: Third exclusive route. Multi-office gap angle.

campaigns.name: Preferred-partner offset variant
campaigns.strategy: Keep {{location_count}} in the first line. Lead with WindoVision's published Preferred Partnerships: other home-service providers on the display that help cover the cost of the system.
campaigns.overview: A/B against the coverage map. Same exclusive route, preferred-partner economics instead of gap-map language.

campaigns.name: 24/7 Lead Window Playbook
campaigns.strategy: Notice the brick-and-mortar office Maps already lists, name the dark-after-hours gap, offer the 24/7 Lead Window Playbook. Soft CTA. Proof: 900+ offices, 30 million+ users, since 2002.
campaigns.overview: Mandatory catch-all for 100% TAM coverage. City and franchise are merge tags only.

campaigns.name: MLS/IDX plus QR variant
campaigns.strategy: Lead with standard IDX feed sync (listings download and come down automatically) plus custom QR codes for listings clients can scan on the go. Do not change routing. Do not invent a conversion rate.
campaigns.value: Live stock, scannable on the sidewalk
campaigns.overview: A/B against the playbook. Still exclusive catch-all, still one TAM.

launchPlan: Pull Google Maps Places for Real estate agency / Real estate office in the United States and Canada. Keep office_name, named_city, franchise_group, website, phone, and a Street View / listing-photo pass for storefront_window_state in the same export. This is the TAM spine. Do not start in Apollo.

Route on storefront_window_state first-match: paper_flyers Tier 1, renovation_or_opening Tier 2, multi_office_gap Tier 3, remaining in-TAM catch-all. Suppress already_customer at office level only. A RE/MAX, KW, or Coldwell Banker logo in the WindoVision gallery is not a franchise-wide exclude.

Fill renovation_or_opening from local news, grand-opening posts, and Maps recency when photos are inconclusive. Cluster multi_office_gap from same-brand name + website + phone. Do not invent a TAM headcount — windovision.com does not publish one.

Resolve Broker/Owner, Principal, Managing Broker, and Office Manager from the office team page, then LinkedIn Sales Navigator with a United States / Canada geo filter. Title is a merge tag, not a second TAM.
Resolve work emails from the office contact page first, then Hunter / Prospeo / Findymail. Apollo last, and only after the office is routed. Do not buy a raw US-real-estate Apollo list.

Launch Tier 1 Paper-to-Pixel Window Brief first. Sharpest visible signal, closest to the paper-versus-live story already on windovision.com. Stale-paper copy as the control, after-hours email/text capture as the A/B on the same list.

Add Tier 2 Fit-Out Storefront Kit once opening and remodel merge tags are clean. Then Tier 3 Portfolio Coverage Map. Turn on the 24/7 Lead Window Playbook catch-all last so every remaining in-TAM office still has a route.

Keep franchise_group, named_city, and buyer_title as merge tags, not campaign splits, until one storefront-signal tier is clearly working. Do not launch a tier under the waterfall SOP contact floor (~1,500 contacts when the TAM allows); that threshold is the SOP, not a WindoVision site number. Do not send Clay-looking openers. The notice line is always the window Maps already shows. Proof in copy stays at 900+, 30 million+ users, and since 2002 — plus attributed homepage quotes as color, never as new GTMx metrics.

Cut or rebuild that tier. Keep the exclusive waterfall. Retune photo-pass labels from the live scrape if a band is starved of contacts.
